_about: Canonical reference list. docs/REFERENCES.md and the site's Sources page are generated from this file (scripts/make_web_data.py). Every efficiency figure carries its exact test conditions. 'status' records how it was verified.

references.title: Fundamentals of Power Electronics, 3rd ed.
references.authors: R. W. Erickson, D. Maksimovic
references.summary: The standard text for conversion ratios, volt-second and charge balance, CCM/DCM boundaries and averaged loss models used throughout the lessons.

references.title: Accurate prediction of ferrite core loss with nonsinusoidal waveforms using only Steinmetz parameters
references.authors: K. Venkatachalam, C. R. Sullivan, T. Abdallah, H. Tacca
references.summary: The improved Generalized Steinmetz Equation (iGSE) used for all inductor core-loss estimates here.

references.title: Analysis and Optimization of Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Converters
references.authors: M. D. Seeman, S. R. Sanders
references.summary: Canonical slow-switching / fast-switching limit (SSL/FSL) output-resistance analysis of switched-capacitor converters.

references.title: A General Method for Analyzing Resonant and Soft-Charging Operation of Switched-Capacitor Converters
references.authors: Y. Lei, R. C. N. Pilawa-Podgurski
references.summary: Shows when adding a single inductor removes the charge-sharing loss (soft charging), the principle behind the flagship's SC region.

references.title: Review of Commercial GaN Power Devices and GaN-Based Converter Design Challenges
references.authors: E. A. Jones, F. Wang, D. Costinett
references.venue: IEEE J. Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics 4(3):707-719
references.summary: Survey of commercial GaN transistors and practical design issues (layout parasitics, gate drive, dynamic on-resistance, thermal).

references.title: Switched-Capacitor-Based Hybrid Resonant Bidirectional Buck-Boost Converter for Improving Energy Harvesting in Photovoltaic Systems
references.authors: C. M. A. da Luz, K. F. A. Okada, A. S. Morais, F. L. Tofoli, E. R. Ribeiro
references.headline: 96 % and 99.2 % (NOT converter efficiency)
references.conditions: Figures are extracted PV power divided by the string's theoretical maximum (energy harvest). Scenario 1: 38.4 W -> 57.6 W; scenario 2: 36 W -> 49.6 W; 1050 W/m^2, 45 C, four-module string of 20 W and 10 W modules, variable-resistor load, 50 kHz, Infineon IPP082N10NF2 MOSFETs. No standalone converter efficiency is reported.
references.summary: A differential-power-processing converter shuffles power between mismatched PV modules so the string recovers most of its available power.

references.title: High efficiency switched capacitor buck-boost converter for PV application
references.authors: Z. Liang, A. Q. Huang, R. Guo
references.conditions: 240 W prototype, 200 V output from a 60-cell module (Vmpp 30 V); fixed-gain resonant SC stage plus a partial-power buck-boost for MPPT; auxiliary inductor for ZVS. Switching frequency and devices not verified.
references.summary: An SC stage does most of the step-up while a small buck-boost trims it for MPPT. The '96-97 % SC buck-boost for PV' figure sometimes quoted could NOT be verified; this is the closest verified paper.

references.title: Analysis and Design of a Condensed Buck-Boost Converter Utilizing Monolithic Bidirectional GaN Switches
references.authors: A. Aron, P. Eliat-Eliat, J. Buonato, S. Coday (MIT)
references.headline: ML-CoBB 95.4 % buck / 97.5 % boost peak; passive weight 2.85x lower than the NIBB
references.conditions: 1 kW-rated 3-level prototype, 200-500 V in, 270 V out, 100 kHz; 95.4 % at 500 -> 270 V and 97.5 % at 200 -> 270 V, both at 880 W. Return-path-inductor variant 97.3 % / 98.1 %. Bidirectional switch: Transphorm TP65F060WS (preliminary part). MEASURED EFFICIENCY EXCLUDES GATE-DRIVE LOSS.
references.summary: Replacing some switches in a flying-capacitor buck-boost with single-chip bidirectional GaN switches cuts inductor weight about 3x at 95-98 % efficiency. News coverage: Power Electronics News, 7 Apr 2026.

references.title: 600W Solar Power Optimizer Reference Design Based on GaN (TIDA-010949)
references.authors: Texas Instruments
references.headline: 99.0 % peak switching; 99.5-99.6 % in pass-through
references.conditions: Four-switch buck-boost with 2x LMG2100R026 GaN half-bridges; 15-80 V in, 0-80 V out, up to 300 kHz. 99.0 % at 600 W, 15 A output (98.6 % at 18 A). 99.5 % (33 V in) and 99.6 % (43 V in) are a SHORT/pass-through state, not conversion. C2000 control-card power is subtracted (auxiliary power excluded). Not peer reviewed.
references.summary: A vendor reference design: a GaN solar power optimizer at about 99 % while actually converting.

references.title: A 400W, 99.3% Efficient GaN Buck-Boost Converter
references.authors: M. Heydari, Q. Huang, A. Q. Huang
references.headline: up to 99.3 % measured
references.conditions: 500 kHz GaN buck-boost, 400 W; ~110 W/cm^3 with one inductor choice, ~35 W/cm^3 with another. Input/output voltages, the exact 99.3 % operating point, device part numbers and gate-drive inclusion were NOT verified (full text inaccessible).
references.summary: A GaN buck-boost at 500 kHz with up to 99.3 % measured efficiency; treat as the best verified ceiling for this class, conditions pending.

references.title: A Spurious-Free Piezoelectric Resonator Based 3.2 kW DC-DC Converter for EV On-Board Chargers
references.authors: E. Stolt, W. D. Braun, K. Nguyen, V. Chulukhadze, R. Lu, J. Rivas-Davila
references.headline: 3.2 kW at 97.7 %; 5.7 kW/cm^3 component power density
references.conditions: 450 V -> 220 V, four paralleled piezoelectric converters, ring-electrode resonator suppressing spurious modes. Resonator material, switching frequency, devices and gate-drive inclusion not verified from the abstract. Research stage.
references.summary: Four vibrating-crystal converters in parallel deliver EV-charger power with no magnetic inductor.

references.title: Enumeration and Analysis of DC-DC Converter Implementations Based on Piezoelectric Resonators
references.authors: J. D. Boles, J. J. Piel, D. J. Perreault
references.headline: >99 % peak (abstract); >= 96 % over a wide range
references.conditions: Prototype 100-200 V in, 40-80 V out, up to ~25 W, 115-135 kHz; APC 790 resonator (APC 844 material, radial mode); EPC2019 GaN; TI UCC27611 driver. The >99 % operating point could not be confirmed as measured (an appendix gives >99 % at 100 V -> 60 V, 4 W, apparently calculated); the measured plot read (Vout = 40 V) shows ~90-98 %. Gate-drive inclusion not stated. Research stage.
references.summary: Systematically lists every way to build a DC-DC converter around a piezoelectric resonator and identifies the high-efficiency switching sequences.
references.status: PARTIAL (bibliographic VERIFIED; the >99 % figure is treated as calculated)

references.title: A hybrid piezoelectric resonator-based DC-DC converter
references.authors: J.-Y. Ko, W.-C. B. Liu, P. P. Mercier (UC San Diego)
references.headline: 96.2 % peak at 48 V -> 4.8 V
references.conditions: 48 V in, 4.8 V out, 150 mA (~0.72 W); 115-129 kHz, inductive region; APC 841 PZT disc 20 mm x 0.25 mm; IC in 180 nm BCD; open-loop control from a C2000 DSP. Gate-drive and control power inclusion not stated. Reports 4x baseline output current and 81.6 % lower resonator current. Research stage.
references.summary: Embedded flying capacitors move the piezo stage's best ratio from 2:1 to 3:1, reaching ~9:1 step-down efficiently.
references.status: VERIFIED (publisher page and PMC full text)

references.title: A Regulated 48V-to-1V/100A 90.9%-Efficient Hybrid Converter for POL Applications in Data Centers and Telecommunication Systems
references.authors: R. Das, H.-P. Le
references.headline: 90.9 % peak at 48 V -> 1 V
references.conditions: Dual-phase multi-inductor hybrid; 90.9 % at 1 V / 30 A (100 A max); 93.6 % at 2 V / 35 A; 95.3 % at 5 V / 40 A; EPC2015c and EPC2023, 1 uH inductors; GATE-DRIVE LOSSES INCLUDED; 440 W/in^3 at 1 V. Frequency partly verified (333 kHz optimal, 167 kHz measured setting).
references.summary: An inductor-plus-capacitor hybrid steps 48 V directly to 1 V for processors at about 91 %.

references.title: A Three-Level Buck-Boost Converter With Planar Coupled Inductor and Common-Mode Noise Suppression
references.authors: Y. Cao, Y. Bai, V. Mitrovic, B. Fan, D. Dong, R. Burgos, D. Boroyevich, R. S. K. Moorthy, M. Chinthavali
references.headline: up to 25 dB common-mode noise reduction; 30 % lower winding loss
references.conditions: 30 kHz, 50 kW bidirectional platform; efficiency figure and exact voltages NOT verified.
references.summary: A three-level (flying-capacitor) buck-boost at 50 kW with a planar coupled inductor: the same topology family as the flagship, at 100x the power.

references.title: 99% Efficient 10 kV SiC-Based 7 kV/400 V DC Transformer for Future Data Centers
references.authors: D. Rothmund, T. Guillod, D. Bortis, J. W. Kolar
references.venue: IEEE J. Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics 7(2)
references.headline: 99.0 % DC-DC
references.conditions: 7 kV DC -> 400 V DC, 25 kW, 48 kHz; 10 kV SiC MOSFETs (Wolfspeed CPM3-10000-0350) and 3x paralleled 1.2 kV C2M0025120D; 99.0 % from 13 to 25.6 kW measured calorimetrically INCLUDING auxiliaries and cooling; 98.1 % for the full solid-state transformer. A series-resonant DC transformer, NOT a flying-capacitor multilevel converter.
references.summary: A single 10 kV SiC stage turns medium-voltage DC into 400 V with about 1 % loss.

references.title: European or CEC efficiency (PVsyst documentation)
references.authors: PVsyst SA
references.headline: CEC = .04n10+.05n20+.12n30+.21n50+.53n75+.05n100; Euro = .03n5+.06n10+.13n20+.10n30+.48n50+.20n100
references.conditions: Secondary source; the primary CEC/Sandia protocol document was not reached. CEC also averages over three DC voltages (not verified here).
references.summary: Weights used for the weighted-efficiency numbers.

references.title: CoolGaN BDS 650 V G5 (IGLT65R055B2, IGLT65R110B2) and 40 V BDS (IGK048B041S)
references.authors: Infineon Technologies
references.conditions: 650 V TOLT parts announced May 2025; 40 V WLCSP part (4.8 mOhm max) available 2026. Neither class fits a 60 V solar input, which is why the flagship uses the Innoscience 100 V part.
references.summary: Commercial monolithic bidirectional GaN switches.

references.title: VGaN bidirectional 100 V switch INV100FQ030C
references.authors: Innoscience
references.conditions: 100 V, 2.5/3.2 mOhm, 100 A, FCQFN 4x6 mm; product page only; gate structure to be confirmed in the datasheet.
references.summary: The only verified 100 V-class monolithic bidirectional GaN switch; used for the flagship's disconnect and bypass.

references.title: Comparison of photovoltaic array maximum power point tracking techniques
references.authors: T. Esram, P. L. Chapman
references.summary: The standard survey of MPPT methods (19 families). The control lab's algorithm families follow its classification.

references.title: Optimization of perturb and observe maximum power point tracking method
references.authors: N. Femia, G. Petrone, G. Spagnuolo, M. Vitelli
references.summary: How to choose the P&O step size and update period against the converter dynamics. Basis of the fixed- and variable-step P&O trackers.

references.title: Maximum photovoltaic power tracking: an algorithm for rapidly changing atmospheric conditions
references.authors: K. H. Hussein, I. Muta, T. Hoshino, M. Osakada
references.venue: IEE Proceedings - Generation, Transmission and Distribution 142(1):59-64
references.summary: Introduces incremental conductance: at the MPP dI/dV = -I/V, so the sign of dI/dV + I/V tells the tracker which side of the peak it is on. In principle it can hold at the peak instead of hunting; in practice it still needs voltage changes to measure dI/dV.
references.status: VERIFIED (Crossref: title, venue, DOI; full author list and pages from Semantic Scholar)

references.title: A variable step size INC MPPT method for PV systems
references.authors: F. Liu, S. Duan, F. Liu, B. Liu, Y. Kang
references.summary: Variable-step incremental conductance: step proportional to |dP/dV|, fast far from the MPP and fine near it.

references.title: Theoretical and experimental analyses of photovoltaic systems with voltage- and current-based maximum power-point tracking
references.authors: M. A. S. Masoum, H. Dehbonei, E. F. Fuchs
references.summary: Fractional open-circuit-voltage and short-circuit-current tracking: cheap, but the Vmpp/Voc ratio drifts with conditions.

references.title: Dynamic maximum power point tracking of photovoltaic arrays using ripple correlation control
references.authors: T. Esram, J. W. Kimball, P. T. Krein, P. L. Chapman, P. Midya
references.summary: Ripple correlation control: correlate the converter's own switching ripple in power and voltage to climb to the MPP. The control lab's extremum-seeking tracker uses the same principle with an injected low-frequency dither (see also Leyva et al. 2006, Brunton et al. 2010).

references.title: Discrete-time ripple correlation control for maximum power point tracking
references.authors: J. W. Kimball, P. T. Krein
references.summary: Sampled-data form of ripple correlation control, suited to digital controllers.

references.title: Maximum power point tracking of multiple photovoltaic arrays: a PSO approach
references.authors: M. Miyatake, M. Veerachary, F. Toriumi, N. Fujii, H. Ko
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems 47(1):367-380
references.summary: Particle swarm optimisation for the global MPP under partial shading. The control lab's swarm uses the standard PSO update with its own tuned coefficients.

references.title: Maximum power point tracking scheme for PV systems operating under partially shaded conditions
references.authors: H. Patel, V. Agarwal
references.summary: Why bypass diodes create multiple maxima, and a global search followed by local tracking: the strategy of the flagship controller.

references.title: Sensorless optimization of dead times in dc-dc converters with synchronous rectifiers
references.authors: V. Yousefzadeh, D. Maksimovic
references.summary: Online dead-time optimisation by minimising input power (via the duty cycle) without extra sensors: the idea behind the adaptive dead-time control.

references.title: Digital multimode buck converter control with loss-minimizing synchronous rectifier adaptation
references.authors: A. V. Peterchev, S. R. Sanders
references.summary: Online loss minimisation and automatic pulse skipping at very light load, the family of controls the burst-mode model belongs to.

references.title: Adaptive digital controller and design considerations for a variable switching frequency voltage regulator
references.authors: W. Al-Hoor, J. A. Abu-Qahouq, L. Huang, W. B. Mikhael, I. Batarseh
references.summary: Adaptive frequency optimisation: a controller that continuously finds the switching frequency with minimum total loss, as the control lab's hill climb does.

references.title: EN 50530:2010 Overall efficiency of grid connected photovoltaic inverters (amended A1:2013)
references.authors: CENELEC
references.summary: Defines dynamic MPPT efficiency (energy drawn / energy available at the MPP) and the irradiance-ramp test sequences: 30-100 % of nominal at 10, 14, 20, 30, 50 and 100 W/m2/s, and 10-50 % at 0.5 to 50 W/m2/s. The control lab's ramp profiles are compressed versions.
references.status: VERIFIED (definition from the standard's free preview; ramp slopes from a Bureau Veritas EN 50530 test certificate; repetition counts not verified)

references.title: MPPT of photovoltaic systems using extremum-seeking control
references.authors: R. Leyva, C. Alonso, I. Queinnec, A. Cid-Pastor, D. Lagrange, L. Martinez-Salamero
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems 42(1):249-258
references.summary: Extremum-seeking control applied to PV maximum power point tracking: perturb, demodulate the power response and integrate the estimated gradient. The basis of the control lab's extremum-seeking tracker.

references.title: Maximum power point tracking for photovoltaic optimization using ripple-based extremum seeking control
references.authors: S. L. Brunton, C. W. Rowley, S. R. Kulkarni, C. Clarkson
references.summary: Extremum seeking that uses the converter's own ripple as the perturbation, linking classical extremum seeking with ripple correlation control.
